candidate.source_a: Calcium phosphate forms crystalline deposits in bone tissue through osteoblast-mediated mineralization.
candidate.source_b: Marine diatoms precipitate silica-based cell walls using enzymatic silicatein proteins.

evidence_assessment.notes: The GLiREL relations are too specific to calcium phosphate and silica-based processes, not capturing the general concept of biomineralization. Source A describes mineralization in bone tissue (calcium phosphate), while Source B describes mineralization in marine diatoms (silica). Both sources independently support the general concept of biomineralization, but neither alone is sufficient as they only provide specific examples.
